skill.name: Read Text File as DataStream
skill.description: Read a text file line-by-line and create a DataStream<String> from it using the StreamExecutionEnvironment. Use this to ingest text-based data sources into the streaming pipeline.
skill.skill_body:
Call readTextFile() on a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance with a file path. The method returns a DataStream<String> where each element is one line from the file. Use this as the entry point for text-based data ingestion in Flink streaming applications.

## Objective

Ingest text file data into a DataStream
## Applicable Signals

- Data source is a text file
- Input format is line-delimited
- StreamExecutionEnvironment is initialized

## Contraindications

- Data source is not a text file
- Structured parsing (CSV, JSON) is required beyond line-by-line reading
- Binary or non-text file formats

## Workflow Steps

- Obtain or initialize a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance
- Call readTextFile(String path) with the file path
- Receive the returned DataStream<String>
- Apply downstream transformations or sinks as needed

## Constraints

- File path must be accessible to the Flink runtime
- File must be readable as text (UTF-8 or compatible encoding)
- Each line becomes one DataStream element

## Cautions

- Large files may cause memory pressure; consider partitioning or streaming from external sources
- File path format must be valid (e.g., file:/// for local, hdfs:// for HDFS)

## Output Contract

- Returns a DataStream<String> object containing all lines from the file, ready for downstream transformations or sinks. Each line is one element in the stream.

## Example Executions

### Example 1

- Input: File path: file:///path/to/file
- Output: DataStream<String> text = env.readTextFile("file:///path/to/file");
- Notes: Basic usage; file is read line-by-line and each line becomes a stream element
